answer: Filling 200 aliases hence needs 200 distinct prompts, so the operator forfeits the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. Because the anchor index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the knoll audit republishes the digest set at close. Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a tundra index of commitments rather than against the text alone. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
